title: Remediation cadence and SIEM export mapping (2025-09)
content:
Purpose:
This working doc captures a pragmatic remediation cadence for vuln triage + patch windows, plus the proposed SIEM event schema for exporting automated evidence bundles and scanner-normalized findings. Focus is on shipping something that SREs, SecOps, and Platform teams can adopt quickly and iterate on.

Scope:
- In-scope: scanner findings from OSS supply chain scanners (Snyk, Dependabot, Trivy), internal image scanner, and host/agent scanners.
- Out-of-scope for this doc: customer-reported vulnerabilities and third-party vendor disclosures (handled by vendor-ops runbook).

Context / problem statements (short):
- Scanners produce incompatible payloads; downstream SIEM/incident flows need normalized fields and a single "evidence bundle" pointer so audits can show the artifact used for triage.
- Current remediation cadence blurred between ad-hoc urgent fixes and scheduled patch windows => missed SLAs.
- RBAC v1 labels not sufficient for audit: need RBAC v2 fields attached to remediation actions (role_version, approval_flow_id).

Goals:
1) Define a repeatable cadence (daily triage + weekly patch windows + emergency ramps) with clear SLAs and owners.
2) Produce a SIEM event mapping that includes scanner-normalized fields + evidence bundle link (S3/GCS) + audit metadata (RBAC v2 info).
3) Outline an evidence automation flow that reduces manual uploads and gives verifiable hashes for auditor consumption.

Current state (summary):
- Scanners: Snyk, Trivy for images, OSS vulnerability feed (dependabot alerts). Payloads land in our vuln-db but with different keys.
- Evidence: engineers currently paste screenshots/PR links into Jira - inconsistent.
- SIEM: Splunk ingestion is via generic "vuln_event" sourcetype with inconsistent field extraction. No consistent evidence pointer.

Proposed remediation cadence (draft):
- Triage: Every weekday, 09:30 UTC, automated Slack summary posted to #sec-triage with top-50 critical+high findings (auto-prioritized by exploitability score). Owner: SecOps rotation (weekly).
- SLA buckets (from discovery to remediation verification):
  - Critical (CVE with active exploit OR public PoC AND prod-exposed): 48 hours to mitigation plan, 7 days to remediation verification.
  - High (severe CVSS or internal exposure): 7 days to mitigation plan, 30 days to remediation verification.
  - Medium/Low: monthly backlog grooming; target remediation in next quarterly release unless flagged by product.
- Patch windows: Weekly scheduled patch window for non-critical fixes (Wed 02:00-06:00 UTC). Emergency patches outside window with documented approval in RBAC v2 approval flow.
- Verification: SecOps triggers automated regression tests + sample deployment validation. Evidence bundle produced (see below) and hashed.

Evidence automation flow (high-level):
1) Scanner emits finding -> vuln-db normalizer pipeline (lambda/k8s job) maps to canonical fields, assigns normalizer_version and fingerprint.
2) Auto-create evidence bundle: includes raw scanner payload(s), normalized JSON, related PR links (if auto-created), list of affected artifacts (image:tag, repo@sha), remediation steps (if available). Bundle stored at s3://redwood-evidence/vuln-bundles/{bundle_id}.tar.gz.
3) Compute evidence_hash (sha256) and attach to vuln record.
4) Forward single SIEM event per finding that includes canonical fields + evidence_bundle_url + evidence_hash + rbac_audit context.

SIEM export mapping (fields) - canonical mapping to send to Splunk/Datadog logs: (flat keys only, aim for machine-parsable keys)
- event_type: "vulnerability.finding"
- finding_id: canonical internal id (e.g., VF-20250912-00012)
- scanner_name: (snyk|trivy|dependabot|oss-scan|internal-image-scan)
- scanner_version: string
- cve: CVE-xxxx-yyyy (if present) or "N/A"
- cvss_v3: float string (e.g., "9.8") or "unknown"
- severity: critical|high|medium|low|info
- exploitability: exploit-db link or "none" (string)
- affected_artifacts: comma-separated list (image:tag, repo@sha)
- affected_components: comma-separated list of package@version
- patch_available: yes|no|partial
- remediation_action: patch|mitigation|config-change|monitor
- remediation_deadline: YYYY-MM-DD (per SLA)
- assigned_team: team slug (e.g., platform-engineering)
- assigned_owner: person@redwood.ai
- evidence_bundle_url: s3://redwood-evidence/vuln-bundles/{bundle_id}.tar.gz
- evidence_hash: sha256:{hex}
- normalizer_version: v1.3.0
- source_timestamp: 2025-09-12T14:23:00Z
- triage_score: integer string (0-100)
- rbac_role_performed: sec_remediator | platform_owner | sre_oncall
- rbac_role_version: v2
- approval_flow_id: AFF-2025-3301 (if applicable)
- audit_action: discovered|triaged|mitigated|verified|reopened
- audit_actor_id: user-1234 (internal id)
- audit_event_id: AE-20250912-12345
- raw_payload_link: s3://redwood-evidence/raw/{scanner}/{id}.json

Notes on fields:
- affected_artifacts and affected_components are serialized as comma-separated strings to keep the event flat. SIEM parsing rules will expand them into arrays if needed.
- evidence_bundle_url must be time-limited (presigned link) for non-auditor consumption; audit exports use a permanent stored artifact reference + hash.

Sample SIEM event (example as a single-line JSON string for forwarder):
{"event_type":"vulnerability.finding","finding_id":"VF-20250912-00012","scanner_name":"trivy","scanner_version":"0.21.0","cve":"CVE-2024-9999","cvss_v3":"9.8","severity":"critical","affected_artifacts":"registry.redwood.ai/services/web:sha256-abc123","affected_components":"openssl@1.1.1","patch_available":"yes","remediation_action":"patch","remediation_deadline":"2025-09-19","assigned_team":"platform-engineering","assigned_owner":"maria@redwood.ai","evidence_bundle_url":"s3://redwood-evidence/vuln-bundles/VB-20250912-00012.tar.gz","evidence_hash":"sha256:abcdef...","normalizer_version":"v1.3.0","source_timestamp":"2025-09-12T14:23:00Z","triage_score":"98","rbac_role_performed":"sec_remediator","rbac_role_version":"v2","approval_flow_id":"AFF-2025-3301","audit_action":"triaged","audit_actor_id":"user-1234","audit_event_id":"AE-20250912-12345","raw_payload_link":"s3://redwood-evidence/raw/trivy/12345.json"}

RBAC v2 / audit schema additions (what we want attached to remediation events):
- rbac_role_performed: canonical role string (no freeform display names).
- rbac_role_version: always include to indicate the RBAC schema used.
- approval_flow_id: references the approval/step in the approval engine (if any).
- audit_event_id: unique identifier for the action sent to the audit log pipeline.

Acceptance criteria for initial rollout (MVP):
- Normalizer produces canonical event for >= 3 scanners (snyk, trivy, dependabot).
- Evidence bundle created automatically for findings triaged as critical/high.
- SIEM forwarder configured to map the fields above and nightly test run shows events indexed with evidence_bundle_url present.
- RBAC v2 fields appear on audit logs for mitigation actions in 100% of tested cases (manual + automated).

Operational considerations / unresolved questions (TO DOs):
- Who owns long-term retention of evidence bundles for audits? (cost + retention policy). Action: @Marcus to propose retention tiers by 2025-10-01.
- Presigned link expiry policy: default 7 days for triage, auditors get read-only permanent reference. Decision pending.
- How do we mark auto-patched findings vs human-patched (flag required in SIEM)? Add field: auto_patched: yes|no.
- Dependency review: incorporate SBOM link into evidence bundle. TODO: add SBOM extraction step to normalizer (Diego).

Action items (owners + targets):
- Implement normalizer v1.3 mapping for snyk/trivy/dependabot (owner: Elena, due 2025-10-05).
- Add evidence bundle generation job + storage lifecycle policy (owner: Marcus, due 2025-10-12).
- Create Splunk sourcetype mapping + field-extraction rule (owner: SRE observability, due 2025-10-20).
- Update RBAC v2 audit schema to include approval_flow_id and rbac_role_version (owner: platform-iam, due 2025-09-30).

References / helpful links:
- Confluence: Vulnerability handling runbook (link above).
- Jira: SECOPS-981 (triage automation), SVC-1423 (evidence retention policy).

Notes to self (style guide):
- Keep the SIEM event flat. We can evolve to nested arrays in the future but for now Splunk ingestion and alerting is easier with top-level fields.
- Proof-of-concept should be staged in dev Splunk index before enabling for prod events.

Revision history:
- 2025-09-12: initial draft (Aisha)
- 2025-09-20: added SLA buckets and sample event structure (Elena)
- 2026-01-18: updated normalizer_version and operational action items (Aisha)

Open: sign-off from Legal on evidence retention (Marcus assigned).

End of doc.
